Now, it’s important to mention that parents who complain about accountability are often just frustrated that everything isn’t going as swimmingly for their child as they’d like.
Simple friendliness (classiness) will help diffuse their frustration and send the message that you’re competent, professional, and someone they can trust.

Every student in this classroom has the right to learn and enjoy school without interference, including yours, and it’s my job to protect that right by enforcing a consequence, as stated in our classroom management plan, every time a student breaks a rule.
Just as you’re consistent with your students, you must be equally consistent with parents.
You're paid to make decisions that are best for students, first and foremost, that protect their freedom to learn in a safe, peaceful, disruption-free, bully-free environment.

t: How Read-Aloud Can Improve Behavior And Instill A Lifelong Love Of Reading
q: Sadly, in recent years, much of the joy of read-aloud has been sucked out and driven away by over-instruction.
We turn works of art into just another academic exercise, destroying the very qualities that draw students into a love of reading.
Once you begin a read-aloud, don’t stop until you run out of time. Don’t stop to analyze the text, explain vocabulary, ask questions, or take breaks for students to discuss.
Honor the story and author and read them from start to finish and as they were intended.
It’s your one guaranteed academic success connection with every student, no matter how much they may be struggling.
Find time for read-aloud every day. Defend it as your one sacred non-negotiable.

The way it works is that after first greeting your students for the day, you're going to take a moment to express your appreciation for them.
It isn’t praise, per se. It’s more of an expression of your gratitude.
I’m happy to be your teacher, and I just wanted you to know that.
It causes a disarming softness, quietness, and ease in their bearing and attitude. It opens their awareness to all that you do for them.
You’re simultaneously fine-tuning, encouraging, and raising the stakes on your classroom tone and tenor while triggering the law of reciprocity that resides in every student.

t: 3 Uniquely Powerful Ways To Praise Your Students
q: There is power in acknowledging true accomplishment with the smallest, simplest gesture.
When the student knows what prompted your praise, there is no reason to say anything at all. In fact, it’s often best if you don’t.
I have former students who still have notes I wrote to them more than 20 years ago.
Because you're recognizing something the student is already feeling inside. You're not overshadowing their accomplishment or disrupting their quiet satisfaction.
Noticing improvement, hard work, or success beyond what your students have done before, and simply noting it—the pure truth of it—can be profoundly meaningful to them.

t: How Today's Students Are Different And What It Means For You
q: Students today are more appreciative, more influenced, and more affected by teachers who are consistently kind and pleasant.
Simple, day-after-day kindness is the one sure way to gain leverage and influence with any group of students, no matter how challenging.
Today’s students are savvy and worldly and have a deep conviction that negative methods of classroom management are not okay with them.
The hard truth is that there is no longer a place for lecturing, scolding, glaring, and the like in an effective teacher’s toolkit.

So many teachers are flailing in the dark, trying out this strategy and that one, never realizing that the reason they struggle with classroom management is that their students privately dislike them.
The good news is that kids are incredibly forgiving—and forgetful.
